insights.headline: Gold rebounds above $4,050 after CPI slide as MCX gains; Fed hike bets cap the rally
insights.summary: Spot gold steadied above $4,050 an ounce after falling nearly 3% to $4,021.36 on hot October US CPI, which rose 0.4% on the month with core up 0.3%, both above forecasts. Traders now price a December Fed hike at close to 100%, with the chance of a half-point move above 10%, while the dollar held near a two-week high and the 10-year Treasury yield topped 5%. On MCX, gold rose Rs 1,009 to Rs 1,41,534 per 10 g and silver jumped Rs 4,147 to Rs 1,86,723 per kg. Indian gold ETFs stayed resilient, the best up about 7.5% in rupees this year as a weaker rupee cushioned the global fall.
points: Spot gold near $4,055 an ounce after falling nearly 3% to $4,021.36; silver held near $52.
October CPI rose 0.4% on the month and core CPI 0.3%, both above forecasts; the BLS published no 12-month change.
Traders price a December Fed hike at close to 100%, with the chance of a half-point move above 10%; the dollar index stood at 102.22.
MCX gold rose Rs 1,009 to Rs 1,41,534 per 10 g and silver jumped Rs 4,147 to Rs 1,86,723 per kg in the morning session.
Indian gold ETFs returned up to 7.5% in rupees this year as a weaker rupee cushioned the global fall.

brief.headline: Gold rebounds above $4,050 but Fed hike bets cap gains
brief.summary: MCX gold rose to Rs 1,41,534 per 10 g as spot gold held above $4,050 after Tuesday's near-3% slide.

bullets.text: Hot October CPI and hawkish Fed remarks drove Tuesday's near-3% slide; Business Standard says priced-in hike bets kept the rebound modest.
MCX silver jumped Rs 4,147 to Rs 1,86,723 per kg, outpacing gold, while a weaker rupee cushioned Indian gold ETFs from the global fall.
Watch: US jobless claims Thursday and October PPI Friday, both at 19:00 IST; Treasury markets shut today for Veterans Day.

trending.title: Gold rebounds but $4,150 caps the recovery
trending.summary: Gold steadied above $4,050 after Tuesday's near-3% slide on hot US CPI, with MCX futures rebounding — but a December Fed hike is priced as close to certain and $4,150 has capped recoveries.

trending.title: Indian gold ETFs beat the global slide
trending.summary: Indian gold ETFs held up far better than global gold in 2026, the best returning about 7.5% in rupees, as a weaker rupee and the import duty rise cushioned the fall in dollar terms.

trending.title: Central banks keep buying — and bringing gold home
trending.summary: China bought 26 tonnes in October and central banks took 321 tonnes in Q3, while European banks moved gold out of US vaults; a Fed note says it reflects sanctions risk, not de-dollarisation.

trending.title: Festive demand holds up as prices cool
trending.summary: A dip in prices drew shoppers to jewellery stores on Dhanteras, with sales holding near last year's level and exchange deals rising to 60-65% of transactions as buyers traded in old jewellery.

items.title: Gold faces inflation headwinds on hawkish Fed tilt; $4,150 stays key hurdle
items.summary: Gold edged above $4,050 an ounce after Tuesday's near-3% slide, as hot October US inflation and hawkish Fed remarks lifted the dollar and Treasury yields. Markets now price a December hike as close to certain, with the chance of a half-point move above 10%, and $4,150 has capped recent recoveries.

items.title: MCX silver jumps over Rs 4,000, Gold rises; What's driving rally on Wednesday?
items.summary: MCX gold futures rose Rs 1,009 to Rs 1,41,534 per 10 g and silver jumped Rs 4,147 to Rs 1,86,723 per kg in the morning session, rebounding after Tuesday's near-3% slide. Spot gold traded near $4,055 an ounce and silver near $52, tracking the global rebound, though hawkish Fed remarks and hot US inflation data still weighed on the metals.

items.title: Gold holds near one-week low as hot US inflation boosts Fed hike bets
items.summary: Gold steadied in early Asian trade after falling nearly 3% in the previous session, with spot gold at $4,039.07 an ounce and silver at $51.52. Hot October US inflation lifted bets on a December Fed rate rise to a 100% chance, with the odds of a half-point move surging, while Fed Vice Chair Bowman stressed that bringing inflation down remains the top priority.

items.title: Gold falls nearly 3% as CPI tops forecasts, lifting dollar and yields
items.summary: Spot gold fell 2.8% to $4,021.36 an ounce, touching a low of $4,015, after hotter-than-expected US October CPI lifted the dollar and Treasury yields and reinforced bets on a bigger December Fed hike. Silver fell more than 3% to $51.72 an ounce, and the 10-year Treasury yield topped 5% as markets fully priced a quarter-point December rise.

items.title: Investors boost odds of half-point Fed hike as core CPI rise meets Waller's bar
items.summary: Odds of a half-point Fed hike in December jumped to about 15% at midmorning after October core CPI rose 0.3%, the level Fed Governor Waller had said would warrant considering a bigger move; a quarter-point rise is now seen as certain, with the 2-year Treasury yield rising the most since early April 2025.

items.title: Global gold price drop 2026: Yellow metal slips 6% in dollar terms, but top Indian gold ETFs still deliver 7.5% returns
items.summary: Gold is down over 6% in dollar terms in 2026 and traded near $4,045 an ounce on 11 November, nearly 30% below its late-January record after ending October at $3,875. Indian gold ETFs held up far better, the best returning about 7.5% in rupees this year, led by 360 ONE Gold ETF at 7.54%, as a weaker rupee cushioned the global fall.

items.title: Fed's Logan calls for two more rate hikes, possibly rapidly
items.summary: Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan said the Fed needs at least two more quarter-point rate hikes, and may need to move promptly, to keep broadening price pressures from taking hold after October core CPI rose 0.3% — a pace that, sustained, would mean annual inflation above 4%. She said the Fed could move more rapidly this winter, then pause to assess, ahead of the December 8-9 meeting.

items.title: Dollar gains traction as Fed speakers warn of risks from inflation
items.summary: The dollar held near a two-week high in early Asian trade, with the dollar index steady at 102.22 after rising 0.5% on Tuesday. Fed funds futures imply a 91.9% chance of a quarter-point December hike and a 9.1% chance of a half-point move, with no pause priced in, as Fed officials warned inflation risks remain.

items.title: Bullion Market Slides In Evening: Gold Drops Below Rs 1,42,000 And Silver Plunges Over Rs 2,000 On MCX
items.summary: MCX gold fell to an evening low of Rs 1,41,815 per 10 g, down Rs 1,351 from the previous close of Rs 1,43,166, and was near Rs 1,42,027 in late evening trade. MCX silver dropped to a low of Rs 1,84,841 per kg, down Rs 2,286, and was near Rs 1,85,104. Retail 24-karat gold was Rs 1,42,470 per 10 g and silver Rs 1,85,820 per kg.

items.title: Why European Central Banks Want Their Gold Back
items.summary: European central banks are stepping up gold repatriation from US vaults as geopolitical tensions strain trust: the Dutch central bank moved about 86 tonnes to London in early September, and the Banque de France now holds all 2,437 tonnes of its gold in Paris. Central banks have bought about 1,000 tonnes a year since 2022.

items.title: Gold reserve repatriations don’t mean central banks are de-dollarizing – Fed’s Weiss
items.summary: A Federal Reserve research note says France, Germany and the Netherlands bringing gold reserves home has barely changed their dollar holdings. France repatriated all its US-held gold in 2025 and early 2026 yet kept a steady 60% dollar share of reserves, and Germany kept its share near 90%. Author Colin Weiss argues custody choices reflect sanctions risk, not de-dollarisation.

items.title: Gold supply falls in Q3 despite record mine production; What happened?
items.summary: Global gold mine output hit a record 1,071 tonnes in the third quarter, up 3% on a year earlier, yet total supply fell 1% to 1,369 tonnes because recycling dropped 8% to 314 tonnes — its lowest since late 2023 — and producers cut hedging by 17 tonnes. Recycling in India stayed depressed, down 12% on the year, and the World Gold Council expects supply to contract slightly in 2026.

items.title: Gold slips below $4,100, silver at $52 as Brent crude falls below $90; Fed rate hike bets rise
items.summary: International gold fell 1.61% to near $4,074 an ounce and silver 1.91% to just above $52 as December Fed hike bets hardened after the hot CPI print. MCX gold futures for December 4 fell 0.78% to Rs 1,42,054 per 10 g and silver 0.75% to Rs 1,85,729 per kg, while Brent crude slipped 3.1% to $89.62, below $90 for the first time since August.

items.title: Silver Outlook Stays Cautious as CPI and Real Yields Remain Firm
items.summary: Silver stayed cautious after the hot US CPI print, with futures near $51.90 and spot around $51.56, below the $55 resistance level and a short-term moving average near $58. FXEmpire notes firm real yields and the stronger December hike case are capping the metal, with $52 as the near-term pivot.

items.title: Gold Prices Fall Rs 500 Amid Strong Dollar, Weak Global Cues
items.summary: Delhi gold fell Rs 500 to Rs 1,46,400 per 10 g on a stronger dollar and weak global cues, while silver held steady at Rs 1,92,500 per kg for a second session. Spot gold fell about 1% to $4,113.55 an ounce and silver over 1% to $52.77, with Brent down 3% to $89.85 as investors awaited US inflation data.

items.title: Customs duty hike takes the shine off organised gold trade; smuggling rises
items.summary: Gold smuggling rose to about 50 tonnes in July-September, more than 16 times the roughly 3 tonnes a year earlier and about 37% of India's 136-tonne total supply, after the import duty rise from 6% to 15%, World Gold Council demand data show. Official bullion imports fell 70% to 64 tonnes, and evading the duty on 1 kg of gold saved about Rs 18.3 lakh, or about Rs 22.5 lakh with GST avoided.

items.title: China buys gold for two straight years as central bank demand remains a key pillar of support
items.summary: China bought 26 tonnes of gold in October, taking its reserves to 2,435 tonnes, just 2 tonnes behind France, and Uzbekistan added 7 tonnes, World Gold Council data show. Central banks bought 321 tonnes in the third quarter, up 42% on the year and well above the five-year quarterly average of 227 tonnes, and the Council expects official buying to stay active.

items.title: Gold, Silver Retreat From Peaks As Bullion Rally Loses Steam
items.summary: Gold and silver pulled back from their MCX contract highs on profit-taking as US rate expectations shifted, with gold down Rs 34,484 per 10 g from a December futures high of Rs 1,77,590 to Monday's close of Rs 1,43,106. Spot gold was at $4,124.42 and silver at $53.22, with traders awaiting US CPI on Tuesday and PPI on Friday.

items.title: Gold falls 21% globally but only 15% in India: How the rupee protected investors
items.summary: Global gold fell 21.4% in dollar terms between January 30 and October 30 while Indian gold fell only 14.9% in rupees, Axis Mutual Fund calculates, with the rupee sliding from about Rs 89 to Rs 96 per dollar in 2026 and the import duty rise to 15% cushioning the domestic fall. 24-karat gold has since rebounded from Rs 1,38,880 per 10 g on November 1 to Rs 1,44,600 on November 9, it reports.

items.title: Decline in gold price pushes jewellery sales on Dhanteras
items.summary: A dip in gold prices drew shoppers to jewellery stores on Dhanteras: Senco Gold reported sales up more than 25% by value with footfall 10-12% higher than last year, and Kalyan Jewellers cut its 22-carat price by Rs 235 a gram to Rs 13,150. Buyers favoured lighter pendants, bangles and chains and smaller gold and silver coins.

items.title: Dhanteras brings cheer to jewellery industry; GJC expects strong wedding demand
items.summary: Jewellery outsold coins on Dhanteras, with sales almost the same as last year, All India Gem and Jewellery Domestic Council vice-chairman Avinash Gupta said, and gold-exchange deals rose to 60-65% of transactions as high prices pushed buyers to trade in old jewellery. Gupta expects fresh bridal buying to dominate a strong wedding season ahead, with 18-carat jewellery gaining wider acceptance.

items.title: ₹1 lakh bought 33 grams of gold on Dhanteras 2016. This year it bought about 7grams
items.summary: At about Rs 30,590 per 10 g on Dhanteras 2016, Rs 1 lakh bought roughly 33 g of 24-carat gold in Delhi; on Dhanteras 2026, at about Rs 1,41,613 per 10 g, the same sum bought about 7.1 g. Business Today calculates the 2016 holding would now be worth about Rs 4.63 lakh, roughly 4.6 times its value.
